report.source_text: Only after persistent and diligent application of the topical Triamcinolone did the patient begin to make substantial progress, to the point where the desquamation and erythema had resolved by day 12 (Figures 10–14).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 56-year-old man presented with diffuse desquamative rash and throbbing pain. Initial labs showed leukocytosis and azotemia. Blood cultures were positive for Staphylococcus aureus, for which he was treated with vancomycin then cefazolin. A skin biopsy revealed psoriasiform hyperplasia with atypical T cell infiltrate and eosinophils. T cell gene rearrangement studies did not show clonal cells, ruling out cutaneous T-cell lymphoma. The patient's symptoms began to improve, and with persistent application of topical Triamcinolone, the desquamation and erythema resolved by day 12.

T cell gene rearrangement studies did not reveal clonal cells, ruling out cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
